items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Walter Crill worked on the Chautauqua shows was supposed to be America's foremost cornetist

ctx.x: In Tuggle Institute. George Hudson that later went into St. Louis and he's still in St. Louis and he played with Jeter-Pillars. Later on after I grew up I played in the band with him. He's in St. Louis as of now, as far as I know, and I started on the trumpet and I tried to play the sax and I tried to play the piano. I didn't know what I was going to do, and - and throughout that my talent of going with the dancing and the singing and what have you, then all these peoples I met. At that particular time - there…

of the band, but nobody had ever led. Jack Hoxey was a terrific cowboy like the Tom Mix here. But he had the One-O-One Ranch and who was the head bandmaster was Edgar Battle, a black man, not a white man. This was something that the Jet, Ebony, and the Pittsburgh Courier and nobody ever wrote about, because he only got - when he got to New Orleans he got writeups in the Picayune. When he got to Cincinnati it was the Cincinnati Inquirer. They said Edgar Battle; they didn't say black man. They said Edgar Battle.…
